title: Queens cannot share a row, column, or diagonal
summary: The left board shows the 11 squares blocked along the row, column, and two diagonals of a single queen, while the right board shows a valid 4-queens solution satisfying all constraints.
context: In chess, a queen attacks pieces at any distance along its horizontal row, vertical column, main diagonal, and antidiagonal. On the 4×4 boards here, rows from top to bottom and columns from left to right are numbered starting at 1 (1-based coordinates).
description: The left board places a queen at row 2, column 2 ((2, 2)); no other square in the same row, column, or either diagonal may hold another queen, ruling out 11 squares across the four directions.
The right board shows a valid arrangement. The two tables below list the squares blocked by the queen on the left board and the column chosen in each row on the right board.

frames.title: Queens cannot share a row, column, or diagonal
frames.explanation: A valid arrangement must satisfy all four constraints simultaneously: distinct rows, distinct columns, distinct main diagonals, and distinct antidiagonals; placing one queen per row avoids row conflicts automatically, leaving column and both diagonal constraints to check.
